jobs.title: Product Manager, Your Private Chef
jobs.description:
About CookUnity:

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the role

Your Private Chef is CookUnity's premium, personalized chef meal service, currently moving from pilot to scale. We're looking for a Product Manager to own YPC end-to-end and to also support the B2B product team as a generalist on other initiatives when needed.

Responsibilities

- Own the YPC roadmap: subscriber personalization, wellness menu verticals (GLP-1, Everyday Wellness, Fitness Fuel, Healthy Heart, Blood Sugar Balance, Kids), and menu recommendation logic.

- Own the chef and recipe pipeline: chef onboarding, recipe intake, tagging, and QA.

- Work with kitchen and vendor partners on ingredient sourcing, costs, and kitchen tooling.

- Manage pricing tiers (standard, premium, extra premium) and unit economics.

- Support the B2B product team more broadly — Smart Fridges, partnerships, integrations — as a generalist when capacity is needed.

- Bring structure to a fast-moving, early-stage product as it expands into new markets.

What success looks like

- YPC has a clear backlog, fewer manual workarounds, and measurable improvements in retention and CSAT.

- The chef/recipe pipeline scales without sacrificing quality or personalization.

- Pricing and vendor economics are transparent and defensible as the product scales.

- Teams have clarity on what we're building, why, and what success means.

- Leadership trusts you with increasingly complex, cross-functional problem spaces.

What we're looking for

Requirements

- 4+ years of experience as a Product Manager.

- Comfortable owning a product end to end, from strategy to execution.

- Strong communicator, works well across stakeholders, engineering, design, ops, and CX.

- Business-minded: cares about retention, margin, and outcomes.

Strong plus

- Passion for wellness, nutrition, or the food-is-medicine space.

- Experience with subscription, personalization, or recommendation-driven products.

- Experience with marketplace/vendor management or culinary/hospitality products.

- Experience taking a product from pilot to multi-market scale.

- Startup or high-growth environment experience.

Benefits

💸 Get paid in USD

🗺 Work remotely: design the life that you want

⛱ Enjoy 15 days of vacation each year from the start date

🎄 16 fully paid Argentinean holidays

🩺 Healthcare Benefit: Monthly stipend to use in your preferred healthcare provider

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises

🧘🏽‍♀️ Flexible benefits, your way: a prepaid card you can use on wellness, learning, food, and more.

🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧑‍🏫 Personalized English coach
If you’re interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you.  Thank you for your time!

CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability.

A quick note for all candidates
We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data)  stay safe while applying to CookUnity.  We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief  “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

- Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:  careers.cookunity.com

- Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official  LinkedIn Company Page .

- We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in  @cookunity.com  and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.

- We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away.

We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

jobs.description:
About CookUnity:

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Role

As a Senior Product Data Analyst , you will be an analytical partner to Product, Design, Engineering, and User Research. You will help teams understand both sides of CookUnity's marketplace: how customers find meals that fit their lives and how chef supply, variety, and merchandising shape that experience. You will own measurement and analysis for a product area, turn ambiguous questions into testable hypotheses, and use evidence to guide product decisions.

Our teams operate through clear success metrics, rapid learning, and controlled experiments. You will help them distinguish meaningful customer and business outcomes from activity, evaluate tradeoffs across the funnel and customer lifecycle, and make insights accessible in day-to-day decisions. This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role with meaningful autonomy and close cross-functional partnership.

What You'll Do in 12 Months

- Make the marketplace easier to discover and more relevant: Study how customers browse chefs, meals, cuisines, dietary options, and price points. Analyze the relationship between local assortment, variety, personalization, and ordering behavior. Help Product identify where better discovery or merchandising can improve repeat ordering and retention.

- Improve the journey from first visit to lasting habit: Map the customer funnel from acquisition through first order, early repeat orders, and longer-term retention. Find friction in onboarding, menu exploration, checkout, and weekly ordering. Segment customers thoughtfully so teams can improve conversion and retention without hiding weak experiences behind averages.

- Measure product bets with credible experiments: Partner with Product and Engineering to define hypotheses, primary metrics, guardrails, sample sizes, and holdouts for changes to the funnel, personalization, loyalty, and in-product interventions. Analyze heterogeneous effects and uncertainty, and recommend whether to launch, iterate, or stop. When a randomized test is impractical, use the strongest available observational approach and explain its limits.

- Connect customer value to marketplace economics: Help teams evaluate how product changes affect order rate, churn, revenue per customer, discounts, chef engagement, and unit economics together. For new categories and ordering formats, define the measures that show whether customers find value and whether the model can scale.

- Reduce the work and stress of ordering: Combine behavioral data with research and customer feedback to understand where subscriptions, delivery information, account management, or support journeys create friction. Measure whether self-service and product improvements solve the underlying problem, not just move contacts to another channel.

- Build a trusted measurement foundation: Define and document product metrics, cohorts, event tracking, and dashboards. Work with Engineering and Data partners to validate instrumentation and maintain reliable behavioral data. Create compelling dashboards that let product teams explore results, spot meaningful patterns, and monitor outcomes after launch.

- Shape a focused learning agenda: Work with Product, Design, and User Research to prioritize the most consequential unknowns, design analyses and tests, and tell a clear story about what the team learned. Share methods and review work with other analysts to raise the quality of product analytics across the team.

What Success Looks Like

- Product teams use clear metrics and guardrails to make decisions about discovery, conversion, ordering, and retention.

- Major launches are supported by credible tests or well-explained evidence, including their impact on different customer segments.

- Insights lead to measurable improvements in customer experience and repeat ordering while accounting for marketplace and financial tradeoffs.

- Stakeholders trust and regularly use self-service reporting, and core behavioral data is sufficiently complete to diagnose product performance.

Core Competences/Requirements

- Approximately 5–7 years in product analytics or a closely related analytical role, with demonstrated ownership of complex analyses and influence on product decisions. Equivalent experience and evidence of impact are welcome.

- Practical fluency with AI tools for accelerating analysis, coding, research synthesis, documentation, and repeatable workflows; able to verify outputs and handle company and customer data responsibly.

- Strong SQL and hands-on experience analyzing large, complex behavioral datasets; ability to validate data and write clear, reusable analyses.

- Practical command of product metrics, funnel and cohort analysis, segmentation, and marketplace or subscription dynamics.

- Experience designing and interpreting A/B tests, including holdouts, guardrails, uncertainty, and tradeoffs; sound judgment about causal claims.

- Ability to turn an ambiguous product problem into a focused learning plan, work independently, and communicate an actionable recommendation.

- Clear data storytelling and constructive partnership with Product, Design, Engineering, User Research, and business teams.

- Ability to build powerful, intuitive dashboards in any tool that answer important product questions, reveal actionable insights, and enable trustworthy self-service analysis.

- Ability to evaluate AI-enabled product experiences through clear success metrics, experiments, user feedback, and appropriate quality and safety checks.

- Curiosity about food, chefs, customer behavior, and the practical constraints of operating a local marketplace.

Benefits

💸 Get paid in USD.

🗺 Work remotely: design the life that you want.

⛱ Enjoy 15 days of vacation each year from the start date.

🎄 16 fully paid Argentinean holidays.

🩺 Healthcare Benefit: Monthly stipend to use in your preferred healthcare provider.

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical.

🐣 Paid family leave.

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises.

🧘🏽‍♀️ Flexible benefits, your way: a prepaid card you can use on wellness, learning, food, and more.

🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧑‍🏫 Personalized English coach.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Sr. Product Manager, Growth to own and optimize our end-to-end acquisition experience—from first impression through checkout—by driving a strategic roadmap and rigorous experiments across landing pages, onboarding, meal selection, and checkout. This role will own key conversion and customer-quality metrics, partnering closely with Growth Marketing to turn traffic into durable business growth.

What You’ll Do

- Own and evolve the product roadmap across First Impressions and Funnel, from landing pages and onboarding through meal selection and checkout

- Analyze acquisition performance, user behavior, and drop-off points to identify opportunities that improve customer quality and funnel efficiency

- Design and run statistically sound experiments across acquisition touchpoints and in-product experiences, balancing rapid tests with foundational investments

- Lead Design and Engineering across First Impressions and Funnel to rapidly ship and iterate on improvements

- Partner closely with Growth Marketing to translate channel strategy, creative, and audience insights into message-matched acquisition experiences

- Own the acquisition customer experience (XP) calendar, ensuring experiments run by other teams do not conflict with Growth team goals or traffic needs.

- Collaborate with CRM and Lifecycle teams to ensure early customer communication supports key friction points and opportunities to re-engage

- Lead cross-functional squads focused on improving first-purchase conversion, acquisition quality, and early retention across every step of the journey

- Drive clear outcome metrics and business cases across conversion, early retention, CAC, LTV, payback, and contribution economics

- Surface insights and learnings regularly with key stakeholders and executive leadership

What Success Looks Like

- Meaningful lift in conversion and acquisition quality from first impression through first purchase

- Shorter time to first meal and increased NPS during trial experience

- Faster learning through rigorous experimentation and scalable experimentation infrastructure

- Cross-functional alignment between product, marketing, and operations around funnel priorities

- Clear measurement and investment framework tied to conversion, retention, CAC efficiency, payback, and contribution impact

What We’re Looking For

- 7+ years of product management or growth-focused experience in a DTC, marketplace, or e-commerce environment, including ownership of consumer acquisition or conversion funnels

- Strong analytical toolkit and comfort using analytics tools (Hex, Tableau, Amplitude, Mixpanel, or similar)

- Proven track record designing statistically sound experiments across user journeys and translating results into product decisions

- Strong commercial judgment and ability to prioritize across customer impact, growth, unit economics, and P&L tradeoffs

- Empathy for customers and a passion for improving product experiences

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills, including direct partnership with Growth or Performance Marketing teams

- Experience in subscription or funnel-driven businesses is a major plus

Technologies You’ll Use

- Mixpanel, SiteSpect, and other solutions

- Snowflake, Hex, and internal data platforms

- Figma (with Design), Jira (with Eng), and Slack (with stakeholders and colleagues.

- Tableau

Learn More About CookUnity

We believe great leadership starts with alignment on vision, values, and ways of working. To give you deeper insight into who we are and what we’re looking for, we invite you to explore:  CookUnity's Leadership Principles  – The values and behaviors that guide how we operate, collaborate, and scale.

We hope this provides valuable insight into our culture and product vision. If this excites you, we’d love to connect!

Benefits

🩺  Health Insurance coverage

🌅 401k Plan

⛱ Unlimited PTO

🗓️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

🐣 Paid Family leave

🕯 Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises

🥘 A generous amount of CookUnity credits to enjoy our amazing meals, added to your account, monthly

🤖 AI-forward workplace: enterprise access to ChatGPT and Claude to help you work smarter and grow faster.

🧘🏽‍♀️ Wellness perks: access to fitness subsidies to build a healthy lifestyle

👩🏾‍🏫 Personalized Spanish coach

🚀 Awesome opportunity to join a company that is looking to change how we eat and how chefs work!

Compensation

All final pay rates will be determined by candidates experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, internal equity, and alignment with market data.

$150,000 — $180,000 USD

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission:  empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, Shopping Experience to own the consumer-facing surfaces that connect eaters with the meals they'll love.

This is the most-trafficked real estate in the product. From the moment a subscriber opens the app to the moment they complete their order, every screen they touch — the home screen, search, menu, collections, product detail pages, and cart — falls within this role's remit. You'll own the product vision, roadmap, and execution across all of it.

You'll work closely with Design, Engineering, Data Science, and Merchandising to make the discovery experience feel effortless, personal, and exciting.

What You'll Do

Own the Discovery Surface End-to-End

- Set and drive the product vision and roadmap across Home Screen, Search, Menu, Swimlanes, Collections, Product Tile & Detail, Cart & Checkout, and Core UI Components.

- Define a coherent discovery experience across web and mobile that scales with catalog complexity and evolving user needs.

- Manage a large, diverse surface area with competing priorities without losing coherence or momentum.

Ship High-Impact Consumer Features

- Partner with Engineering and Design to build, iterate, and launch features that meaningfully improve how eaters find and choose meals.

- Own the product layer of CookUnity's server-driven UI (SDUI) system — thinking critically about how the component architecture enables flexibility for merchandisers while maintaining a great eater experience.

- Drive experimentation across discovery surfaces with rigorous metric frameworks.

Elevate the UX

- Partner tightly with Design to create discovery experiences that reduce friction, build confidence, and feel intuitive across every entry point.

- Own the quality and consistency of core UI components (loading states, error screens, coachmarks, modals) as a shared foundation across the product.

- Maintain a high bar for mobile and web parity, while allowing for platform-native patterns where they matter.

Navigate the Frontend/Intelligence Seam

- Work as a close counterpart to the Sr. PM, Personalization & AI — jointly owning decisions that live at the intersection of how surfaces are designed and what intelligence powers them.

- Translate what the personalization and AI systems are capable of into frontend experiences that make that intelligence visible and useful to eaters.

- Bring a clear point of view to surface-level decisions even when the upstream inputs are probabilistic, evolving, or contested.

Drive Measurable Business Impact

- Improve conversion across browse surfaces (home, search, swimlanes, collections, full menu).

- Reduce checkout abandonment and cart-to-order friction.

- Lift overall funnel CVR and contribution to weekly order frequency and reduction of subscriber churn.

You Are

- A senior, frontend-first product thinker with deep instincts for consumer UX and a track record of owning high-traffic discovery or browsing surfaces.

- Comfortable holding a wide, complex surface area — you can zoom out to set coherent strategy across many screens while staying close enough to the details to make good product decisions.

- A strong design partner who can elevate the quality of an experience, not just spec it.

- Technically grounded enough to work fluently with frontend engineers, understand component architecture, and reason about how system-level decisions affect the user experience.

- Genuinely excited by the challenge of making a large, dynamic food catalog feel simple and delightful to browse.

- Collaborative and low-ego at the seam between your work and adjacent PM domains; you know how to maintain shared ownership without losing accountability.

- Rigorous about experimentation and metrics without being paralyzed by them.

Qualifications

- 8+ years of product management experience, including meaningful ownership of consumer-facing mobile and/or web surfaces at scale.

- Demonstrated experience with discovery, browsing, search, or shopping experiences, ideally in a marketplace or catalog-heavy product.

- Strong UX instincts and a proven track record of close collaboration with design teams.

- Comfortable with frontend product systems (component libraries, server-driven UI, feature flags) and able to partner effectively with frontend engineers.

- Experience running A/B experiments, defining metrics, and making data-informed decisions in ambiguous situations.

- Excellent cross-functional communication; able to influence design, engineering, and business stakeholders across a complex organization.

- Proven ability to manage a large roadmap across multiple surfaces simultaneously.

- Manage a large, diverse surface area with competing priorities without losing coherence or momentum.

Ship High-Impact Consumer Features

- Partner with Engineering and Design to build, iterate, and launch features that meaningfully improve how eaters find and choose meals.

- Own the product layer of CookUnity's server-driven UI (SDUI) system — thinking critically about how the component architecture enables flexibility for merchandisers while maintaining a great eater experience.

- Drive experimentation across discovery surfaces with rigorous metric frameworks.

Elevate the UX

- Partner tightly with Design to create discovery experiences that reduce friction, build confidence, and feel intuitive across every entry point.

- Maintain a high bar for mobile and web parity, while allowing for platform-native patterns where they matter.

- Work as a close counterpart to the Sr. PM, Personalization & AI — jointly owning decisions that live at the intersection of how surfaces are designed and what intelligence powers them.

- Translate what the personalization and AI systems are capable of into frontend experiences that make that intelligence visible and useful to eaters.

- Bring a clear point of view to surface-level decisions even when the upstream inputs are probabilistic, evolving, or contested.

- Improve conversion across browse surfaces (home, search, swimlanes, collections, full menu).

- Reduce checkout abandonment and cart-to-order friction.

- Lift overall funnel CVR and contribution to weekly order frequency and reduction of subscriber churn.

- A strong design partner who can elevate the quality of an experience, not just spec it.

- Technically grounded enough to work fluently with frontend engineers, understand component architecture, and reason about how system-level decisions affect the user experience.

- Genuinely excited by the challenge of making a large, dynamic food catalog feel simple and delightful to browse.

- Collaborative and low-ego at the seam between your work and adjacent PM domains; you know how to maintain shared ownership without losing accountability.

- Rigorous about experimentation and metrics without being paralyzed by them.

- Demonstrated experience with discovery, browsing, search, or shopping experiences, ideally in a marketplace or catalog-heavy product.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

The Role

CookUnity is looking for a Staff Product Manager to own our ChefTech team and lead the direction of ChefOS Platform, the product chefs use to run their business with us.

ChefTech is the chef relationship and content layer of our operation. It covers how chefs join the platform, how their recipes become sellable products on our menus, and the tools they use every day: the Chef Portal, the chef mobile app, and the business surfaces where chefs manage their ratings, sales, payouts, and performance.

The broader mandate is ChefOS Platform. A chef's experience with us currently lives across several separate tools. This role owns the vision for bringing them into one product: a single place where a chef handles onboarding, recipes and menu, kitchen operations, and the performance and pay that come out of all of it. It's a wider vantage point than any single squad, drawing on work that runs across the operation and pulling it into one experience for the chef.

There's a larger ambition behind this. We believe the platform we build for our own chefs can become a modular, white-label product for other restaurants and food businesses. That work is greenfield. It calls for someone who can set product direction in open territory, where the problem itself still has to be defined.

This is an individual contributor role. You'll partner closely with Design and Engineering, and there's room to grow a team beneath you over time as the platform scales.

What You'll Do

Own the ChefTech product surface

- Set the roadmap and OKRs for chef onboarding, recipe and product activation, the Chef Portal, and the chef mobile app, and deliver against them each cycle.

- Own these products end to end, from the problem through launch, adoption, and the iterations that follow.

- Partner with Engineering and Design to build and improve the tools chefs use to run their business with us.

Know the chef deeply

- Build a direct line to chefs through interviews, surveys, and ongoing conversation, and use it to understand their needs and where the tools fall short.

- Anticipate what chefs need before it surfaces as a problem, and turn that understanding into product direction.

- Spend real time with chefs using the tools, so each iteration is grounded in how they actually work.

Lead the ChefOS Platform vision

- Define what a unified chef platform looks like and build the multi-quarter plan to get there.

- Pull the separate chef tools into a single, connected product.

- Make the case for platform investments and secure the resourcing to deliver them.

Shape the greenfield opportunity

- Develop the direction for turning the platform into a modular, white-label offering for restaurants and food businesses.

- Set strategy in areas where no precedent exists and the problem is still open.

- Frame large, ambiguous problems in a way the rest of the organization can build against.

Prototype and keep improving how you work

- Build prototypes to test ideas early and cheaply, before committing to a full build.

- Use AI across your workflow (prototyping, drafting, research, analysis) and keep experimenting with it to work faster and improve the quality of your output.

Drive measurable impact

- Own the outcomes that matter to chefs: how quickly they onboard, how smoothly their recipes reach the menu, how much of the toolset they adopt, and how well the platform supports their business.

- Define how success will be measured before the build starts, so impact is provable.

- Surface progress, risk, and results to senior leadership.

You Are

- Experienced owning product at the platform or multi-product level, able to hold a wide, connected surface without losing the thread.

- Comfortable setting direction when the problem is undefined and there's no precedent to lean on.

- Effective at moving work across teams you don't manage, through influence and clear alignment.

- Low-ego at the seams between your work and adjacent teams, without letting accountability blur.

- Trusted for your judgment by senior stakeholders, and sought out when a hard problem needs framing.

Qualifications

- 10+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a platform or several connected product lines rather than a single feature area.

- A track record of 0-to-1 work: taking on large, undefined problems and setting direction where there was none.

- Experience leading complex, multi-team programs that required aligning and influencing teams you didn't own.

- Product judgment that senior stakeholders trust as an input to strategy.

- Ability to break down big, ambiguous problems and give others a way to reason about them.

- Excellent communication across engineering, operations, and executive audiences, including turning cross-team conflict into decisions that hold.

- Comfortable using AI tools in your product work, with a habit of experimenting to work faster and better.

- This role requires regular in-person travel to the US.

- Bonus: experience with operational, supply chain, marketplace, or B2B platform products, or packaging an internal platform into a product for external customers.

About the Team:

The Strategic Partnerships team builds and scales CookUnity’s most important external relationships — health and wellness brands, connected health platforms, fitness apps, and other partners who share our belief that what you eat is foundational to how you feel. We sit at the intersection of product, commercial, and operations, turning partnership agreements into real product experiences that drive member growth and retention.

The role:

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager, Strategic Partnerships to own the full picture for CookUnity’s health and wellness brand partnerships: the go-to-market strategy that gets each partnership off the ground, the external relationships that keep them healthy, and the product roadmap and integration architecture that makes them work at scale.

You are the bridge between external partner teams and CookUnity’s internal product and engineering org. You translate commercial agreements into shipped product, own the partner relationship from launch onward, and synthesize learnings across partners to build infrastructure that makes every future partnership faster and better.

Responsibilities:

Go-to-Market & Partner Launch

- Define the launch strategy for each new partnership — messaging, activation plan, launch milestones, and success metrics

- Work with marketing and brand partners on co-branded campaigns, member communications, and channel activation

- Set and track launch KPIs; run post-launch reviews to identify what’s working and what to iterate on

- Build partnership launch playbooks that make each new partner go-live smoother and faster than the last

Partner Relationship Management

- Serve as CookUnity’s primary product point of contact for external partners — the person they call when something’s working and when it isn’t

- Run regular partner touchpoints: product reviews, roadmap alignment sessions, and quarterly business reviews

- Manage partner expectations, escalations, and change requests with clear communication and follow-through

- Represent CookUnity at partner on-sites, industry events, and executive meetings

Partner Product Experiences

- Own the product roadmap for all partner-facing surfaces: co-branded landing pages, benefit redemption flows, member eligibility verification, partner onboarding, and referral attribution

- Partner closely with internal CookUnity PMs who own those surface areas to prioritize partnership work within their engineering team’s scope

- Design seamless, high-converting experiences for customers who come to CookUnity through health and wellness brand partners

- Run A/B tests on partner-specific acquisition and activation flows to improve conversion, time-to-first-meal, and early retention

Integration Infrastructure

- Own the product strategy for CookUnity’s partner integration platform — APIs, SSO, referral and attribution systems, and data exchange flows

- Translate partnership agreements and commercial commitments into clear product requirements and technical scopes

- Work with engineering and external partner tech teams to ship clean, scalable integrations with clear SLAs and ownership

- Build integration playbooks and scalable frameworks so that onboarding the next partner is faster and more predictable than the last

Partner Insights & Growth

- Define the measurement framework for partnership channel performance: partner-sourced acquisition, activation, retention, and LTV

- Identify opportunities to turn integrations from one-time technical connections into compounding growth and retention levers

- Surface partner learnings back into CookUnity’s core product roadmap — if health and wellness members behave differently, that insight should shape what we build

Qualifications:

- 7+ years of product management experience, with meaningful exposure to partner integrations, platform products, or marketplace environments

- Proven experience owning external partner relationships — you’ve been the primary point of contact for a strategic partner and know how to manage expectations, run business reviews, and resolve escalations

- GTM chops: you’ve launched partnerships or products and can own the strategy from commercial agreement to live activation

- Experience translating external partnership or BD agreements into product requirements and shipped product

- Strong analytical instincts — comfortable defining metrics, running experiments, and using data to prioritize

- Excellent cross-functional skills: you can align engineering, design, ops, and external partners around shared outcomes without having direct authority over any of them

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and bringing structure to early-stage, fast-moving partnership models

- Strong written and verbal communication — you’ll regularly interface with both external stakeholders and internal leadership

- Ability to leverage generative AI to increase output quality and speed.

Preferred requirements:

- Experience in health and wellness, insurance benefits, employer perks, or adjacent spaces

- Background with API product management, integration platforms, or developer-facing products

- Experience at a marketplace, DTC subscription, or platform company

- Familiarity with referral and attribution systems, SSO, or member eligibility verification

We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data)  stay safe while applying to CookUnity.  We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief  “proof of humanity” to confirm that we’re connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

- Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page:  careers.cookunity.com

- Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you’re unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official  LinkedIn Company Page .

- We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in  @cookunity.com  and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.

- We’ll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don’t share any information and let us know right away.

If something ever feels off or you’re unsure about a message, we’d much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.
